SPECIFICATION FOR 
WOODEN SETTING CAT FOR TWoImEN CROSS CUT SAWS 



1. Scope — Specifies the material, dimensions and other requirements of wooden setting cat used 
for setting of two-men cross cut saws specified in IS : 12127-1987 'Specification for two-rnen ero$8 cut 
saws'. 

2. Material 

2.1 Wooden Cat — Shall be made from any good quality properly seasoned carpentry wood. 
2.1.1 The wooden blanks shall be free from knots, decay ( rot ), splits, borer holes, etc. 

2.2 Nails — Shall be made of mild steel [ see IS : 226-197^ Specification for structural steel ( standard 
quality ) ( fiftti revision ) ]. 



3. Shape and Dimensions — Shall be as shown in Fig, t.

3,1 Tolerance on the dimensions shall be very coarse class specified in IS : 2102 ( Part i )-1980 'General 
tolerances for dimensions and form and position: Part i General tolerances for linear and angular 
dimensions ( second revision )'. 

4. Other Requirements — The nails shall be tight fit. The tip of the nails shall be flat, 

5. Workmanship and Finish — The wooden setting cat shall be free from burrs and other defects 
detrimental to their normal use and shall be smooth finished.

7. tfarklng — Each wooden setting cat shall be legibly and indelibly stamped with Xh$ manufacturer's 
name m trade-mark and the batch or code number. 

7.1 Standard Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

8. Packing — Shall be as agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser. 

8. Sampling — Unless otherwise agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser, the sampling 
plan and criteria for conformity as given in Appendix A shall be followed. 



APPENDIX A 

(Claused) 
SCALE OF SAMPLING AND CRitElllA FOR CONFORMITY 

A>1. Scala of Sampling 

A-1.1 Lot — in any consignment, all the setting cats manufactured under similar conditions of 
manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. 

A*1.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of this specification, tests shall be 
carried out from setting cats selected from each lot separately. The number of setting cats to be 
sdected at random from a lot shall be in accordance with Table 1. To ensure the randomness of 
selection, the procedure as laid down in IS ; 4905-1968 'Methods for random sampling' shall be 
followed. 

TABLE 1 SAMPLE SIZE AND PEKMlSSiaLE NUMBER OF DEFECTIVES

A-2. Numbsr of T«ste and Criteria for Conformity 

A-2.1 The setting cats selected according to A-1.2 shall be examined for material ( see 2), dimensions 
( see 3 ) and general requirements (see 4 and 6 ). Any setting cat failing to rneet the requirement for 
any one or more of the characteristics mentioned above shall be declared defective. 

A-2.1. 1 The lot shall be considered conforming to requirements of the characteristics mentioned 
above if the number of setting cats found defective is less than or equal to the corresponding number 
given Table 1. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

Wooden setting cats are used for checking the setting of teeth in two-men cross cut saws 
( both peg toothed and raker toothed ). 

In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from the Logging Development 
Division. Forest Research Institute and Colleges, Dehra Dun.
